questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To value the rich heritage of our composite culture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote co-operative societies**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens are listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution, which was added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**. 
• The Fundamental Duties include several obligations such as safeguarding the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India, promoting harmony, and valuing the rich heritage of the country. 
• **To promote co-operative societies** is not mentioned among the Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A. *Hence, this option is correct.* 
• The duty **to protect the integrity of India** is explicitly included under the Fundamental Duties, emphasizing the importance of national unity and security. *This is correct.* 
• Similarly, duties like **valuing the rich heritage of our composite culture** and **developing a scientific temper** are also part of the Fundamental Duties aimed at fostering intellectual and cultural development. *These are correct.* 
• The Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law; however, they serve as moral obligations for citizens to uphold the spirit of the Constitution. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Fundamental Duties:** 
• The Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the **USSR** and were introduced in India to remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation. 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51A. 
• Examples include respecting the Constitution, the National Flag, and the National Anthem, promoting harmony, and protecting the environment. 
• The **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, added the 11th duty, which obligates parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children or wards aged 6 to 14 years. 
• **Key Characteristics of Fundamental Duties:** 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be legally enforced by the courts. 
• They are considered essential for promoting a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens towards the nation. 
• The duties aim to ensure that citizens actively participate in the process of nation-building and uphold the democratic values of the country. 
• **Comparison with Fundamental Rights:** 
• While Fundamental Rights empower citizens, Fundamental Duties remind them of their responsibilities. 
• Both Fundamental Rights and Duties are essential for maintaining the balance between individual liberty and societal interests. 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties was one of the significant recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**. 
• **Examples of Fundamental Duties:** 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions. 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom. 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so. 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife. 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence. </ul

questions.question:
As of 31st July 2025, which of the following country is the member of BIMSTEC?

I. Thailand

II. Iran
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIMSTEC** stands for **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**, comprising countries dependent on the Bay of Bengal for trade and economic cooperation.
 
• The member countries of BIMSTEC as of **31st July 2025** are **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Thailand**.
 
• **Thailand** is one of the founding members of BIMSTEC, established on **6th June 1997**. Hence, **Statement I is correct.**
 
• **Iran** is not a member of BIMSTEC. It is geographically located outside the Bay of Bengal region and has no affiliation with BIMSTEC as of the given date. Hence, **Statement II is incorrect.**
 
• BIMSTEC primarily aims to foster cooperation in areas like trade, investment, energy, technology, and tourism among member countries in the Bay of Bengal region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **BIMSTEC Establishment:**

 
 
• BIMSTEC was established through the **Bangkok Declaration** on **6th June 1997** with initial members including Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand.
 
• Later, Myanmar joined in **December 1997**, Nepal and Bhutan joined in **February 2004**.
 
 
 
• **Key Objectives of BIMSTEC:**
 
 
• To enhance regional cooperation among member countries in the Bay of Bengal region.
 
• To promote economic growth and sustainable development through mutual collaboration.
 
• To strengthen connectivity, trade, and investment among member nations.
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas of BIMSTEC Cooperation:**
 
 
• Major focus areas include **trade and investment, technology, energy, transportation and communication, tourism, fisheries, agriculture, public health, poverty alleviation**, and **climate change adaptation**.
 
• Special emphasis is laid on improving connectivity in the region via infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Differences with SAARC:**
 
 
• BIMSTEC is seen as an alternative to **SAARC**, focusing exclusively on regional cooperation without political conflicts.
 
• Unlike SAARC, BIMSTEC excludes Pakistan, which makes it a preferred platform for India to strengthen regional ties.
 
 
 
• **Recent Developments:**
 
 
• The **5th BIMSTEC Summit** was held on **30th March 2022** in Colombo, Sri Lanka, where member countries agreed to enhance cooperation in various sectors.
 
• India emphasized the importance of **regional connectivity** and the implementation of the BIMSTEC Master Plan for Transport Connectivity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Member Countries:**

 
 
• India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Thailand.
 
• These countries represent a significant portion of the global population and economy in the Bay of Bengal region.
 
 
 
• **BIMSTEC Secretariat:**
 
 
• The BIMSTEC Secretariat is located in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**.
 
• It was established in **2014** to coordinate and monitor BIMSTEC activities.
 
 
 
• **Connectivity Projects:**
 
 
• Projects like the **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project** aim to enhance connectivity between India and Myanmar.
 
• Efforts are underway to establish a **BIMSTEC Free Trade Area** (FTA) to boost trade and economic cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Future Agenda:**
 
 
• Strengthening institutional mechanisms and enhancing cooperation in priority sectors.
 
• Promoting people-to-people contact and cultural exchange among member nations.

questions.question: The International Solar Alliance is a collaborative initiative between India and ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**France**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **The International Solar Alliance (ISA)** is a joint initiative launched by **India and France** during the 21st session of the Conference of the Parties (COP-21) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in Paris on **30th November 2015**. 
• The primary aim of the ISA is to promote the use of **solar energy**, facilitate energy access, and help in reducing dependence on fossil fuels to combat climate change. 
• It is a coalition of **solar resource-rich countries** that lie fully or partially between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, although other countries can also join the alliance. 
• ISA focuses on key areas such as **scaling solar applications** for agricultural use, scaling solar mini-grids, and scaling rooftop solar installations. 
• The headquarters of the ISA is located in **Gurugram, India**, and it is the first international intergovernmental organization to have its headquarters in India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Objectives of the International Solar Alliance:** 
• To reduce the cost of solar energy and its components through bulk purchase and local manufacturing. 
• To mobilize financial resources for the development of solar energy projects in member countries. 
• To promote research and development in solar energy and its applications. 
• To increase the use of solar technologies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote sustainable development. 
• **Key Initiatives under ISA:** 
• **One Sun, One World, One Grid:** This initiative aims to interconnect solar energy grids across countries to ensure a reliable supply of clean energy globally. 
• **STAR-C program:** Aims to develop solar technology application and research centers across member countries. 
• **Affordable Finance at Scale:** Seeks to lower the cost of capital for solar projects by leveraging international public finance. 
• **France’s Role in ISA:** 
• France has been a key partner of India in this initiative, providing technical and financial support to operationalize the ISA framework. 
• The French Development Agency (AFD) has committed significant financial resources to support solar energy projects under the ISA initiative. 
• **Partnerships and Membership:** 
• As of 2023, **124 countries** have signed the ISA framework agreement, out of which more than 90 have ratified it. 
• Major partners include the European Union, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), and the World Bank. 
• **Milestones Achieved:** 
• The ISA has launched several global programs, such as the **Affordable Solar Power for Agriculture** and **Scaling Solar Applications for Agricultural Use (SSAAU)**. 
• It has been instrumental in mobilizing investments in **solar energy infrastructure** across developing countries.

questions.question: Who among the following is the first Indian woman mountaineer to climb Mount Everest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bachendri Pal**__.

__

• **Bachendri Pal** became the **first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest** on **23rd May 1984**.

• She was a part of the **Indian expedition to Mount Everest** in 1984, which was organized by the **Indian Mountaineering Foundation**.

• Her achievement marked a significant milestone in Indian mountaineering history and inspired many women in India to pursue mountaineering.

• Bachendri Pal hails from a small village in Uttarkashi district of **Uttarakhand** and is known for her determination and perseverance.

• She has been honored with several awards for her achievement, including the **Padma Shri** in 1984 and the **Arjuna Award** in 1986.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Ruma Pal:** 

• Ruma Pal is a renowned legal personality and served as a **judge of the Supreme Court of India**.

• She has no association with mountaineering or climbing Mount Everest.

• **Cornelia Sorabji:** 

• Cornelia Sorabji was the **first woman to practice law in India**.

• She is known for her contributions to the legal field and women's rights but has no connection with mountaineering.

• **Shikha Sharma:** 

• Shikha Sharma is a well-known Indian banker and the former Managing Director & CEO of **Axis Bank**.

• She is not related to mountaineering or climbing Mount Everest.

• **Legacy of Bachendri Pal:** 

• After her Everest expedition, she continued to inspire young mountaineers by leading several expeditions, including the **First All-Women Trans-Himalayan Expedition** in 1997.

• She served as the director of the **Tata Steel Adventure Foundation**, promoting adventure sports and mountaineering in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **First Indian Woman on Everest:** Bachendri Pal’s achievement made her a national icon, showcasing the potential of Indian women in adventure sports.

• **Awards and Recognition:** Apart from the Padma Shri and Arjuna Award, she has also received the **National Adventure Award**.

• **Inspiration:** Her success encouraged many Indian women to take up mountaineering and adventure sports, breaking societal stereotypes.

• **Mount Everest Facts:** Mount Everest, with an elevation of **8,848.86 meters**, is the highest peak in the world, located in the **Himalayas on the Nepal-China border**.

questions.question: In January 2025, who has been appointed as the India's new Ambassador to Israel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jitender Pal Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Jitender Pal Singh** has been appointed as India's new Ambassador to Israel in **January 2025**.

• The appointment comes amidst strengthening diplomatic relations between **India and Israel**, focusing on areas such as **technology, defense, agriculture, and innovation.**

• Ambassadors play a crucial role in representing India's interests in foreign countries and fostering bilateral cooperation.

• India and Israel have shared a strong relationship since the establishment of diplomatic ties in **1992**, with collaborations in sectors like **counter-terrorism, water management, and cybersecurity.**

• The role of an ambassador involves facilitating agreements, coordinating diplomatic missions, and promoting cultural exchange between the two nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **India-Israel Relations:**

• India officially recognized Israel in **1950**, but formal diplomatic ties were established in **1992**.

• Key areas of collaboration include **defense technology**, agricultural advancements, and strategic partnerships in combating terrorism.

• In **2017**, Indian Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** became the first Indian PM to visit Israel, further strengthening bilateral ties.

• **Role of Ambassadors:**

• An ambassador is the highest-ranking diplomat representing their nation in a foreign country.

• They are responsible for promoting economic, cultural, and political interests and maintaining bilateral relations.

• Ambassadors coordinate negotiations, treaties, and agreements between nations.

• **Israel's Importance to India:**

• Israel is one of India's leading partners in the defense sector, supplying cutting-edge military technology.

• India imports agricultural innovations, water management technologies, and cybersecurity tools from Israel.

• Israel is also a key player in India's energy and renewable energy initiatives.

• **Diplomatic Appointments:**

• Diplomatic appointments are decided by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) in India.

• Such appointments are crucial in strengthening global partnerships and advancing India's foreign policy objectives.

• Ambassadors are often chosen based on their expertise in foreign relations and their ability to represent India effectively on international platforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **India-Israel Defense Collaboration:**

• India is the largest buyer of Israeli military equipment, ranging from drones to missile defense systems.

• Israel has supported India's defense modernization efforts and provides joint research and development opportunities.

• **Strategic Cooperation:**

• Both countries collaborate on counter-terrorism strategies and intelligence sharing to combat global security challenges.

• Israel has supported India on issues like border security and fighting terrorism in international forums.

• **Agricultural and Water Management:**

• Israel's drip irrigation and water recycling technologies have been widely adopted in India to improve agricultural productivity.

• Joint projects focus on enhancing rural livelihoods and combating water scarcity issues.

</ul

questions.question: In Janaury 2025, The Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) of NITI Aayog launched _______.

 __

• This initiative focuses on equipping women with **business mentoring, skill enhancement, and market linkages** to help them establish and grow their ventures. 
• The program also emphasizes **financial inclusion**, enabling women entrepreneurs to access loans, grants, and other financial assistance required to scale their businesses. 
• Through partnerships with various stakeholders, including the corporate sector, non-profits, and government agencies, the initiative ensures a **comprehensive ecosystem** for women entrepreneurship development. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __

• It provides **information, mentorship, and funding support** tailored to the needs of women-led businesses. 
• The platform collaborates with industry leaders, financial institutions, and non-profits to foster entrepreneurship among women.

• Focuses on **capacity building, financial literacy, and market access**. 
• Encourages participation from women in **rural and semi-urban areas**. 
• Includes training modules on **digital marketing, e-commerce, and business management**.

• **Stand-Up India:** Facilitates bank loans between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore to women entrepreneurs. 
• **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY):** Provides financial support to small business owners, including women. 
• **Importance of Women Entrepreneurship:** 
• Encourages **economic independence** and empowers women to contribute to the nation’s GDP. 
• Drives **innovation** and enhances **job creation** opportunities in various sectors. 
• Helps in achieving **gender equality** and reducing the gender gap in the workforce. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Empowering Women through Entrepreneurship:**

• **Networking Opportunities:** Women entrepreneurs are connected with mentors, industry leaders, and peers. 
• **Skill Development:** Training modules ensure that women entrepreneurs are equipped with modern business practices.

questions.question: Prime Minister's Internship Scheme (PMIS) aims to provide _________ crore young Indians with 12-month paid internships in the nation's top companies over the next five years.

 __ 
• The **Prime Minister's Internship Scheme (PMIS)** is an ambitious program launched by the Government of India to provide youth with meaningful employment opportunities. 
• The scheme aims to provide **1 crore young Indians** with 12-month paid internships in the nation's top companies over the next five years. 
• It is designed to equip Indian youth with **practical skills and corporate exposure** to enhance their employability and professional growth. 
• The program will partner with leading companies across India, ensuring a variety of industrial sectors are covered, including IT, manufacturing, education, healthcare, and more. 
• The initiative aligns with the government's broader goal of addressing **youth unemployment** and encouraging skill development as part of India's demographic dividend. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __

• To ensure the participation of India's corporate sector in addressing the unemployment challenge. 
• To provide interns with a stipend and financial support during their internship tenure. 
• **Eligibility Criteria:** 
• Applicants should be **Indian nationals** aged between 18 and 30 years. 
• They must have at least completed their **secondary education** or an equivalent qualification.

• **Global Context:** Several countries, including the USA and Germany, have implemented similar internship programs to bridge the gap between education and employment. 
• **Skill Development in India:** The PMIS complements other initiatives like **Skill India** and **National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme** (NAPS). 
• **Monitoring and Evaluation:** The scheme will be monitored by a dedicated government task force to ensure its effectiveness and scalability. </ul

questions.question: In July 2025, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana has completed how many years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 years**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** was launched on **15 July 2015** by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). This aligns with the celebration of World Youth Skills Day. 
• By **July 2025**, the scheme will have completed **10 years** of its implementation, focusing on skill development and employability enhancement. 
• The primary objective of PMKVY is to **enable youth to take up industry-relevant skill training** that will help them secure better livelihood opportunities. 
• The scheme operates under the **Skill India Mission**, aiming to train over 40 crore people in India by 2022 in different skills. 
• PMKVY is implemented by the **National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)**, which acts as a nodal agency for monitoring and coordinating the program. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Key Components of PMKVY:** 
• **Short Term Training (STT):** Aimed at school/college dropouts and unemployed youth, providing industry-relevant skills training aligned with the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF). 
• **Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL):** This component assesses and certifies individuals with existing skills and prior experience. 
• **Special Projects:** This component allows for the creation of projects to address skill requirements in regions or sectors that are not covered under standard PMKVY courses. 
• **Placement Assistance:** Successful candidates are provided placement opportunities through Training Partners under the scheme. 
• **Achievements of PMKVY:** 
• As of 2023, over **1.37 crore individuals** have received training under PMKVY across various sectors and disciplines. 
• The scheme has significantly contributed to bridging the skill gap in industries such as IT, construction, healthcare, and automotive sectors. 
• Many beneficiaries of PMKVY have successfully secured employment or started their entrepreneurial ventures. 
• **Skill India Mission:** 
• Launched in **2015**, the mission aims to create a skilled workforce in India to meet the demands of a growing economy. 
• Under this mission, several initiatives like PMKVY, Udaan, and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) have been introduced. 
• It aligns with the government's focus on **‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’** by promoting self-reliance and skill development. 
• **Global Perspective:**

questions.question: A designated portion of a relay race is called as _______.
questions.solution:

__
 
• A **leg** refers to a designated portion or segment of a relay race. It is a critical term used in athletics to divide the race into sections for each team member.
 
• In a relay race, the total distance is divided into equal segments called "legs," which are run by individual team members.
 
• The performance in each **leg** contributes to the overall team result in the relay race. A strong performance by all runners ensures a higher chance of winning.
 
• Relay races commonly include 4x100 meters or 4x400 meters, where each runner completes a specific **leg** before passing the baton to the next runner.
 
• This term is specific to athletics and is not interchangeable with other options provided, such as "heat," which refers to a qualifying race, or "spikes," which are shoes worn by athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relay Races:**

 
 
• Relay races are team events in track and field where four athletes complete equal segments of the race, passing a baton to the next runner after completing their respective leg.
 
• The two most common relay events are the **4x100 meters** and **4x400 meters**. In the 4x100 meters relay, each runner covers 100 meters, while in the 4x400 meters relay, each runner covers 400 meters.
 
• Relay races require precise coordination during baton exchanges to avoid disqualification.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Terms:**
 
 
• **Heat:** Refers to a preliminary race used to qualify athletes for the final race. It is not related to a portion of the relay race.
 
• **Spikes:** Specialized shoes with spikes on the sole to provide better grip and traction on the track, aiding in faster sprints.
 
• **Lifting:** This term is unrelated to athletics and is typically associated with weightlifting or the act of picking something up.
 
 
 
• **History of Relay Races:**
 
 
• The concept of relay races originates from ancient Greece, where messengers ran in relays to deliver messages over long distances.
 
• Modern relay races became part of the Olympic Games in the early 20th century, with the 4x100m and 4x400m events introduced in 1912.
 
 
 
• **Rules and Techniques:**
 
 
• Each runner must run entirely within their designated lane during their leg of the race, particularly in the 4x100 meters relay.
 
• The baton must be passed within a designated zone of 20 meters, and dropping the baton or passing it outside this zone leads to disqualification.
 
• In the 4x400 meters relay, runners may merge into the innermost lane after the first leg is completed.

questions.question: The 'Tapu' dance is traditionally performed by tribes belonging to which Indian state?

questions.question: Which of the following bill provides details on the imposition, abolition, or regulation of taxes proposed in the budget?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Bill** is a legislative proposal presented in Parliament along with the Union Budget to give effect to the financial proposals for the upcoming financial year.
 
• It contains provisions related to the **imposition, abolition, or alteration of taxes**, as proposed in the Union Budget.
 
• The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** as per Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, meaning it is primarily concerned with taxation and government spending.
 
• The Bill needs to be passed by the Lok Sabha and can only be discussed but not amended by the Rajya Sabha, as per the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The passage of the Finance Bill is crucial for implementing the financial proposals of the government, including tax amendments and budgetary allocations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Private Member Bill:**

 
 
• A Private Member Bill is introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a minister.
 
• It is used to propose new laws or amendments to existing laws but is not related to financial matters.
 
• Only a small fraction of private member bills are passed in Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Constitution Amendment Bill:**
 
 
• This bill is introduced to amend the Constitution of India under Article 368.
 
• It requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament and, in some cases, ratification by half of the state legislatures.
 
• It is not related to the imposition or abolition of taxes.
 
 
 
• **Ordinary Bill:**
 
 
• An Ordinary Bill is concerned with any matter other than financial or constitutional amendments.
 
• It can be introduced in either House of Parliament and does not require a special procedure for its passage.
 
• It is not used for tax-related proposals or budget implementation.
 
 
 
• **Money Bill:**
 
 
• A Money Bill is a subset of the Finance Bill and deals only with provisions mentioned in Article 110 of the Constitution, such as taxation, government borrowing, or expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• It is certified as a Money Bill by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Finance Bill encompasses a broader scope than a Money Bill, including tax-related and non-tax-related financial proposals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Stages of the Finance Bill:**

 
 
• The Finance Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha during the presentation of the Union Budget.
 
• It is debated and voted upon after the General Budget discussion is completed.
 
• The Bill must be passed within 75 days of its introduction, as per constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations to the Finance Bill but cannot amend or reject it.
 
• The Lok Sabha may accept or reject these recommendations.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Finance Bill and Appropriation Bill:**
 
 
• The Finance Bill deals with taxation and financial proposals, while the Appropriation Bill authorizes the government to withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• Both are essential for implementing the Union Budget.

questions.question:
As per the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management. Act-2003, the actual deficits may exceed the targets only on which of the following ground?

I. National security

II. National calamity
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 (FRBM Act)** was enacted by the Government of India to institutionalize financial discipline, reduce fiscal deficit, and improve macroeconomic management.
 
• As per the provisions of the FRBM Act, the central government is required to set annual targets to reduce fiscal deficits and eliminate revenue deficits.
 
• However, **Section 4(2) of the FRBM Act** provides for certain exceptions where the fiscal deficit targets can be exceeded. These are:
 
 
• **National Security:** In situations where national security is threatened, the government may breach the deficit target. This is deemed a valid exception. *Hence, Statement I is correct.*
 
• **National Calamity:** In the event of a severe national calamity (such as natural disasters), the government is allowed to exceed the prescribed fiscal deficit target to address the crisis effectively. *Hence, Statement II is correct.*
 
 
 
• The exceptions ensure that the government has the flexibility to respond to extraordinary circumstances without being constrained by fiscal deficit limits.
 
• It is important to note that these deviations must be approved by Parliament, and the government is required to present a detailed explanation for breaching the fiscal targets.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003:**

 
 
• The FRBM Act was enacted to ensure responsible fiscal management and achieve long-term macroeconomic stability.
 
• The Act includes measures such as reducing the fiscal deficit to a specified target (e.g., 3% of GDP) and eliminating the revenue deficit over time.
 
• The objective is to boost public savings, reduce inflationary pressures, and maintain sustainable debt levels.
 
• It applies to both the central government and state governments, although states have their own versions of FRBM laws.
 
 
 
• **Provisions for Deviation under FRBM Act:**
 
 
• Deviation from deficit targets is permissible under exceptional circumstances such as war, national security threats, natural calamities, or other extraordinary events.
 
• The government must provide a detailed explanation to Parliament when deviating from set targets, including measures to return to the prescribed path.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the FRBM Act:**
 
 
• The Act has been amended several times, including the **2018 amendment**, which introduced a fiscal deficit glide path and mandated the establishment of a **Fiscal Council**.
 
• The fiscal deficit target was revised to a more flexible range, allowing for economic uncertainties.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic:**
 
 
• The fiscal rules under the FRBM Act were temporarily relaxed during the COVID-19 pandemic to allow the government to undertake higher spending to address the health and economic crisis.
 
• This highlighted the importance of having flexibility in fiscal management policies during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• India's fiscal deficit for FY 2022-23 was projected at **6.4% of GDP**, reflecting higher government expenditure due to economic recovery measures.
 
• The FRBM Act emphasizes transparency and accountability in fiscal management by requiring the government to present fiscal policy statements and medium-term fiscal frameworks to Parliament.

questions.question: _______ in Bihar was the capital of Magadha for several years. Later the capital was shifted to Pataliputra
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajagriha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Rajagriha**, now known as Rajgir in Bihar, was the **first capital of the Magadha Empire**.

• It served as the capital for several years before the capital was shifted to **Pataliputra (modern-day Patna)**.

• Rajagriha, meaning "House of the King," was strategically located amidst five hills, which provided it with natural fortification and made it an important center of political and cultural significance.

• The city is associated with the early teachings of both **Buddhism and Jainism**. Lord Buddha spent several years in Rajagriha, and it was here that King Bimbisara of Magadha met Buddha and became his follower.

• **Historical records and archaeological evidence** indicate that Rajagriha was an important hub of activity during the reigns of rulers like Bimbisara and Ajatashatru.

• The shift to Pataliputra was made due to its more central location and better opportunities for trade, transportation, and military strategy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Pataliputra (Patna):**

• **Pataliputra** was established as the capital of Magadha during the reign of King Ajatashatru. It later became the center of major political activities in ancient India.

• It flourished as a cultural and administrative center under the Mauryan and Gupta Empires.

• Notable rulers like Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka made Pataliputra their capital, and it became famous for its grand architecture and urban planning.

• **Other Options:**

• **Ujjain:** Ujjain, located in modern-day Madhya Pradesh, was a prominent city in ancient India but never served as the capital of Magadha. It was a major center of trade, learning, and spirituality.

• **Vaishali:** Vaishali, also in Bihar, was the capital of the Vajji confederacy and holds significance in Jain and Buddhist traditions. It was not the capital of Magadha.

• **Taxila:** Located in present-day Pakistan, Taxila was a center of learning and an important city in the Gandhara region. It was not associated with Magadha.

• **Importance of Magadha:**

• Magadha was one of the most powerful Mahajanapadas in ancient India, known for its military strength, strategic location, and economic prosperity.

• The Magadha Empire laid the foundation for later empires like the Mauryan and Gupta dynasties, which significantly influenced Indian history.

• **Buddhism and Jainism in Rajagriha:**

• Rajagriha was an early center for Buddhism and Jainism. It is said to be the location of the first Buddhist Council, which was held after the death of Buddha.

• Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, also spent considerable time in Rajagriha, spreading his teachings.

• **Geographical and Strategic Importance:**

• Rajagriha's location amidst five hills provided natural defense against invasions, making it a secure capital for Magadha.

• The fertile plains around the city contributed to the economic prosperity of the Magadha Empire.

questions.question:
Which Veda contains hymns mostly taken from the Rigveda, arranged for singing?

I. Samaveda

II. Yajurveda
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samaveda**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **The Samaveda** primarily consists of hymns and melodies that have been taken from the **Rigveda**. These hymns are specifically arranged for chanting and singing during rituals. 
• It is one of the four Vedas—**Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda**—and is regarded as the "Veda of melodies and chants." 
• The hymns of the Samaveda are chanted during **religious rituals and sacrifices** to invoke divine blessings. It is closely associated with the practice of **Soma rituals**. 
• Unlike the Rigveda, which focuses on the poetic aspect of hymns, the Samaveda emphasizes the **musical rendition** of these hymns, making it a unique collection of Vedic literature. 
• While many hymns in the Samaveda are borrowed from the Rigveda, their arrangement and purpose in the Samaveda are distinct, as they are meant to be sung rather than recited. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Rigveda:** 
• The Rigveda is the **oldest** of the four Vedas and consists of hymns that focus on the praise of various deities such as Agni, Indra, and Varuna. 
• It is written in **Sanskrit** and is considered one of the most ancient religious texts in the world. 
• The Rigveda contains a total of **1,028 hymns** divided into 10 books called Mandalas. 
• Its focus is on the poetic and philosophical aspects of Vedic literature. 
• **Yajurveda:** 
• The Yajurveda is primarily a compilation of **prose and verses** designed to guide the performance of rituals and sacrifices. 
• It is divided into two parts: the **Shukla (White) Yajurveda** and the **Krishna (Black) Yajurveda**. 
• Unlike the Samaveda, the Yajurveda focuses more on the procedural and practical aspects of conducting Vedic rituals. 
• **Atharvaveda:** 
• The Atharvaveda is considered the **Veda of knowledge** and includes hymns, spells, and incantations for practical purposes like healing, marriage, and protection against evils. 
• It is distinct from the other three Vedas in its focus on the everyday concerns of life rather than rituals. 
• **Samaveda's Unique Features:** 
• The Samaveda is often referred to as the "Book of Chants" due to its emphasis on **musical notations**. 
• It is regarded as the origin of Indian classical music and has had a profound influence on its development. 
• Priests who specialize in the Samaveda are called **Udgatris**, and they play a key role in chanting during rituals. 
• **Important Points:** 
• The **Samaveda** is closely associated with the **Sama Gana**, the singing style of Vedic hymns used during rituals. 
• It is especially used in **Soma Yajnas**, where Soma, a sacred plant, is offered to deities. 
• The Samaveda has contributed significantly to the cultural and spiritual heritage of India.
